> If so, would it not also be possible to achieve this by deactivating the kinematic sensors when not monitoring?

I put up another PR to show what this looks like: #106490

I just updated my solution to also respect the case in which only the body callback is present. Since I was mainly looking at this issue from an `Area3D` perspective, I previously overlooked that scenario.

But I think that @mihe's solution might still be a bit nicer in case it has the same effect as making the body static :)

> @jrouwe What exactly is the optimization at play with static sensors? Is it simply that they will be inactive/asleep and therefore won't detect any collisions between eachother? If so, would it not also be possible to achieve this by deactivating the kinematic sensors when not monitoring? A quick test seems to suggest that's the case, but I'm not sure what other side effects it might have.

I think it helps to understand the 'find body pairs' loop. Basically this loop loops over all active bodies and checks for collisions against all other bodies (active and non active). The function you mention is determining which things will hit. So for an active sensor against an active body, this function will be called twice (Sensor/Body and Body/Sensor) and it should return true only once (which is what the second half of the function ensures).

Both PRs in this ticket have the effect of removing the sensor from the active body list, meaning that the for loop will no longer visit the sensor. So the only way this sensor can now detect other bodies is if that other body is active so that it will be visited by the for loop. This means that in both cases sleeping bodies will no longer be detected, which is probably not what you wanted.

If you want to disable sensor vs sensor collisions but retain sensor vs sleeping bodies then the sensor should remain kinematic and active. To disable sensor vs sensor you should either put the sensor in an `ObjectLayer` that doesn't collide with other sensors or you should adjust the `GroupFilter` to filter out the collisions so that this if returns false:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c3ae6aa10b1c0c5488cf5b5e82dd34d265c1567c/thirdparty/jolt_physics/Jolt/Physics/Body/Body.inl#L75-L76

> If you want to disable sensor vs sensor collisions but retain sensor vs sleeping bodies then the sensor should remain kinematic and active. To disable sensor vs sensor you should either put the sensor in an `ObjectLayer` that doesn't collide with other sensors or you should adjust the `GroupFilter` to filter out the collisions so that this if returns false:

Based on this feedback, the preferred options would then be to either

1) add extra layers for non-monitoring areas that do not collide with each other, or
2) add conditions to the methods used by the `JoltGroupFilter` to reject irrelevant, i.e., non-monitoring, area/area (and probably also area/body?) pairs,

correct?

I feel like updating the `can_monitor` methods in `JoltArea3D` to also check if at least one of the areas in a pair is monitoring might be the simplest approach, since it does not require any modification of the overall layer setup. Would that be an acceptable change, @mihe?

> This means that in both cases sleeping bodies will no longer be detected, which is probably not what you wanted.

This is in fact what we want. Disabling `monitoring` on an `Area3D` should disable monitoring of all objects, not just other areas.

If I'm understanding you correctly, it sounds like making the kinematic sensor inactive (i.e. #106490) would indeed serve the same purpose as what this PR does, which means both would retain the current functionality while optimizing away needless collision checks between non-monitoring sensors.

I am somewhat partial to #106490, since it would mean not needing to introduce different motion types for `Area3D`.

There might however still be some argument for adding a `has_body_monitor_callback()` check to `JoltArea3D::can_monitor(const JoltBody3D &p_other)`, since we're probably still performing unnecessary collision checks against physics bodies. I'm having trouble reasoning about the implications of that right now though, so I'd prefer to leave that for a separate PR. I've run into weird bugs before when making these checks too aggressive.

> it sounds like making the kinematic sensor inactive (i.e. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106490) would indeed serve the same purpose as what this PR does, which means both would retain the current functionality while optimizing away needless collision checks between non-monitoring sensors.

Just making the kinematic sensor inactive does not disable collisions completely. It only disables them with static or inactive objects. An active dynamic body would still be detected by an inactive kinematic sensor. An active kinematic sensor would still detect inactive kinematic sensors.

> Just making the kinematic sensor inactive does not disable collisions completely. It only disables them with static or inactive objects. [...] An active kinematic sensor would still detect inactive kinematic sensors.

That is again largely what we're after here. We want non-monitoring sensors to not collide with other non-monitoring sensors, i.e. inactive versus inactive sensors. Even if `Area3D.monitoring` is disabled, you can still have `Area3D.monitorable` enabled, meaning active/monitoring sensors should still be able to collide with inactive/non-monitoring (but monitorable) sensors.

(I've implemented `Area3D.monitorable` as a [separate broad-phase layer](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/be3ecaeb3c51433058ad4e96ec892d18f4291efd/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_broad_phase_layer.h#L44-L45), so disabling that property gets taken care of at that level instead.)

> An active dynamic body would still be detected by an inactive kinematic sensor.

That would be the `JoltArea3D::can_monitor(const JoltBody3D &p_other)` part I mentioned above, which gets called from the group filter. I went ahead and pushed that change to #106490. So now collisions between inactive/non-monitoring sensors and active bodies will be filtered out at the group filter level. I need to test that part thoroughly, but theoretically it should be fine I guess.

I also threw in the same change for `JoltArea3D::can_monitor(const JoltArea3D &p_other)`, even though that check is presumably entirely redundant, since both areas would need to be non-monitoring for that code to ever be relevant, but they'll never get to the point of calling the group filter in such a scenario, since they'll both be inactive.
Ok, I think I understand now and I think that #106490 will work 🤞
Closed since #106490 was accepted as fix for #106482. Thanks for the quick solution, @mihe and @jrouwe !
